title: Cotton Board Rules and Regulations: Adjusting Supplemental Assessment on Imports (2025 Amendments)

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Threatened Species Status With Section 4(d) Rule for White Sands Pupfish and Critical Habitat Determination
snippet: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the White Sands pupfish (Cyprinodon tularosa), a fish species from southcentral New Mexico, as a threatened species with protective regulations under section 4(d) of the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the White Sands pupfish. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. All areas meeting the definition of critical habitat for the White Sands pupfish occur on Department of War (DoW) owned facilities and are exempt from designation as critical habitat in accordance with section 4(a)(3)(B) of the Act. Therefore, we are not proposing any areas as critical habitat for the White Sands pupfish.

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for Mazama Newt
snippet: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the Mazama newt (Taricha granulosa mazamae), an amphibian species from the Crater Lake caldera in Crater Lake National Park in Klamath County, Oregon, as an endangered species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the Mazama newt. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. We find that designating critical habitat for this species is not determinable at this time.

title: Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors
snippet: In this interim final rule (IFR), the Department of Commerce is establishing new rules to prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on U.S. technology to threaten U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. First, this rule establishes new restrictions which will apply for exports, reexports, or transfers (in-country) to overseas data centers that remotely supply significant volumes of compute to companies headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau. These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models. Data centers, foreign foundries, and chip exporters are required to perform robust due diligence on their customers, including any direct or indirect ownership or control by persons in Country Group D:5 or Macau, as part of complying with this new control. The license requirement will not apply to commercial recommender systems, such as those used by online retailers or social media companies, as these functions do not pose the same national security threat. Second, in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil (and any additional country designated by the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of State or the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs)--countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion. The license requirement for these five countries will not apply to semiconductors destined to companies headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent company is headquartered in, the United States, provided certain reporting requirements are met. Commerce will be actively monitoring for countries that tolerate evasion of this IFR and will consider a range of consequences for such countries, such as import restrictions, new license requirements on advanced semiconductor exports, downgrading the country's status in the U.S. export control regime, and Entity List designations and temporary export prohibitions for foreign persons involved in such activities. Third, this IFR amends the presumptions which front-end chips fabricators and chip packagers face when exporting advanced-node logic chips. These amendments reduce the number of pathways to overcome the presumptions for chip designers located in destinations which face a license requirement for SI chips. This change gives the U.S. government critical oversight over companies headquartered in certain countries that seek to leverage advanced semiconductor production capabilities in third countries. Finally, the IFR formally rescinds the regulations implementing the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule. The AI Diffusion Rule has never been enforced. The regulatory changes in this rule formalize the rescission of the AI Diffusion Rule, which the Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced in May 2025.

title: Marine Mammals; Proposed Incidental Harassment Authorization for the Southern Beaufort Sea Stock of Polar Bears During Exploration Activities in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge 1002 Area Alaska; Draft Environmental Assessment
snippet: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, in response to a request under the Marine Mammal Protection Act from the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA), propose to authorize nonlethal incidental take by harassment of small numbers of Southern Beaufort Sea (SBS) polar bears (Ursus maritimus) for 1 year from the date of issuance of the incidental harassment authorization (IHA). The applicant requested this authorization for take by harassment that may result from activities associated with a seismic exploration program in the Coastal Plain of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge Section 1002 area. This proposed authorization, if finalized, will be take of polar bears associated with the specified activities, which may come from the SBS stock. We invite comments on the proposed IHA and accompanying draft environmental assessment from the public, Tribes, and local, State, and Federal agencies.

title: Certain Spectral Flow Cytometry Systems and Components Thereof; Notice of Institution of Investigation
snippet: Notice is hereby given that a complaint was filed with the U.S. International Trade Commission on October 8, 2026, under section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended, on behalf of Cytek Biosciences, Inc. of Fremont, California. A supplement to the complaint was filed on October 26, 2026. The complaint, as supplemented, alleges violations of section 337 based upon the importation into the United States, the sale for importation, and the sale within the United States after importation of certain spectral flow cytometry systems and components thereof by reason of the infringement of certain claims of U.S. Patent No. 12,754,128 ("the '128 patent"); U.S. Patent No. 12,487,167 ("the '167 patent"); and U.S. Patent No. 10,739,245 ("the '245 patent"). The complaint further alleges that an industry in the United States exists as required by the applicable Federal Statute. The complainant requests that the Commission institute an investigation and, after the investigation, issue a limited exclusion order and cease and desist orders.

snippet: The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) determines that Navneet Education Limited (Navneet) made sales of paper file folders from India in the United States at prices below normal value (NV) during the period of review (POR) May 17, 2023, through October 31, 2024.

title: Certain Oil Country Tubular Goods From the Republic of Korea: Final Results of Antidumping Duty Administrative Review; 2023-2024; Correction
snippet: The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) published a notice in the Federal Register of September 24, 2026, in which Commerce issued the final results of the 2023-2024 administrative review of the antidumping order on certain oil country tubular goods (OCTG) from the Republic of Korea (Korea). In that notice, Commerce identified two incorrect weighted-average dumping margins, the margin for NEXTEEL Co., Ltd. and the margin for the non-examined companies.

title: Certain Frozen Fish Fillets From the Socialist Republic of Vietnam: Preliminary Results and Rescission, in Part, of Antidumping Duty Administrative Review; 2024-2025
snippet: The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) preliminarily determines that Bien Dong Seafood Co., Ltd. (Bien Dong) and Nam Viet Corporation (NAVICO) made sales of subject merchandise at less than normal value during the period of review (POR), August 1, 2024, through July 31, 2025. In addition, we are rescinding the review with respect to 117 companies. Interested parties are invited to comment on these preliminary results of review.

title: Certain Spectral Flow Cytometry Systems and Components Thereof; Notice of Institution of Investigation
snippet: Notice is hereby given that a complaint was filed with the U.S. International Trade Commission on October 8, 2026, under section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended, on behalf of Cytek Biosciences, Inc. of Fremont, California. A supplement to the complaint was filed on October 26, 2026. The complaint, as supplemented, alleges violations of section 337 based upon the importation into the United States, the sale for importation, and the sale within the United States after importation of certain spectral flow cytometry systems and components thereof by reason of the infringement of certain claims of U.S. Patent No. 12,754,128 ("the '128 patent"); U.S. Patent No. 12,487,167 ("the '167 patent"); and U.S. Patent No. 10,739,245 ("the '245 patent"). The complaint further alleges that an industry in the United States exists as required by the applicable Federal Statute. The complainant requests that the Commission institute an investigation and, after the investigation, issue a limited exclusion order and cease and desist orders.

title: Diamond Sawblades and Parts Thereof From the People's Republic of China: Continuation of Antidumping Duty Order
snippet: As a result of the determinations by the U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) and the U.S. International Trade Commission (ITC) that revocation of the antidumping duty (AD) order on diamond sawblades and parts thereof (diamond sawblades) from the People's Republic of China (China) would likely lead to the continuation or recurrence of dumping and material injury to an industry in the United States, Commerce is publishing a notice of continuation of this AD order.

title: Notice of Scope Ruling Applications Filed in Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Proceedings
snippet: The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) received scope ruling applications, requesting that scope inquiries be conducted to determine whether identified products are covered by the scope of antidumping duty (AD) and/or countervailing duty (CVD) orders and that Commerce issue scope rulings pursuant to those inquiries. In accordance with Commerce's regulations, we are notifying the public of the filing of the scope ruling applications listed below in the month of September 2026.

title: Common Alloy Aluminum Sheet From the Kingdom of Bahrain: Final Results of Antidumping Duty Administrative Review; 2024-2025
snippet: The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) finds that Gulf Aluminium Rolling Mill B.S.C. (GARMCO) subject to this administrative review made sales of common alloy aluminum sheet (aluminum sheet) from the Kingdom of Bahrain (Bahrain) at less than normal value during the period of review (POR) April 1, 2024, through March 31, 2025.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Dassault Aviation Airplanes
snippet: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Dassault Aviation Model FALCON 6X airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a determination that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This proposed AD would require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
